title: Recording: Oh Woman, Oh Why, Monkberry Moon Delight by Paul and Linda McCartney | 1970
content:
Studio B, CBS Studio Building, New York City
Producers: Paul McCartney, Linda McCartney

Paul McCartney worked on two songs on 3 November 1970: ‘Oh Woman, Oh Why’ and ‘Monkberry Moon Delight’.

‘Oh Woman, Oh Why’ had been rehearsed in the studio the previous day. During this session the backing track was completed, with McCartney and Hugh McCracken on electric guitars, and Denny Seiwell on drums. The song became the b-side of his debut solo single.

McCartney and McCracken then double-tracked their guitar lines, including slide guitar by McCracken, and Seiwell added a shaker part.

It remains one of my favorite tracks from that period. The drums’ sound was amazing, one of the best from CBS Studios. It was not a jam, Paul brought the tune in and Spinozza [sic] played electric. Then Paul and I played shakers and percussion.
Denny Seiwell
Paul McCartney Recording Sessions (1969-2013), Luca Perasi

In the afternoon their attention turned to a new song, ‘Monkberry Moon Delight’, which was destined for the Ram album.

It had McCartney on piano, McCracken on electric guitar, and Seiwell on drums. Despite half a day’s work, a master take was not achieved and it was left for another day.

Page last updated: 8 November 2025
